title: Errands
goal: Get everyday jobs done around town on your own: take out cash, sort out a SIM card, get your phone fixed, clothes stitched and ironed, your hair cut and a parcel sent.
intro:
Living somewhere means errands: the ATM with no cash, the phone that's given up, the outfit at the tailor's before Navratri, the pile of shirts for the ironing man, the parcel for your cousin in Surat. In Gujarat most of these jobs are done for you by someone at a small local shop, and the key verb for that is the **causative**: not **કરવું** 'do' but **કરાવવું** 'get it done'.

In this unit you'll learn to say what you need to get done, who you get to do it, and to ask the question every errand ends with: **ક્યારે તૈયાર થશે?** 'When will it be ready?'

grammar.title: Getting something done: the causative -આવ- / -ડાવ-
grammar.body:
English says *I got my hair cut* or *I had my phone fixed*. Gujarati does it with one verb: add **-આવ-** to the root and the verb means 'have someone else do it'.

કરવું 'do' → **કરાવવું** 'get done'
કાપવું 'cut' → **કપાવવું** 'get cut'
મોકલવું 'send' → **મોકલાવવું** 'get sent'
ખોલવું 'open' → **ખોલાવવું** 'get opened'
બદલવું 'change' → **બદલાવવું** 'get changed / replaced'

A long **ā** in the root usually gets shorter: કાપ → **કપાવ**.

Roots that end in a **vowel**, and verbs that already end in **-આવ-**, add **-ડાવ-** (or -વડાવ-) instead:
ધોવું 'wash' → **ધોવડાવવું** 'get washed'
સીવવું 'stitch' → **સિવડાવવું** 'get stitched' (ī → i)
બનાવવું 'make' → **બનાવડાવવું** 'get made'

**Who does the work** takes **પાસે**: મેં **દરજી પાસે** શર્ટ સિવડાવ્યું 'I had the tailor stitch a shirt'. Usually you just leave the person out.

The causative is an ordinary transitive verb: in the past it takes the ergative (મેં, તેં, એણે…) and agrees with the **object**: મેં ફોન રિપેર **કરાવ્યો** (ફોન m), મેં સ્ક્રીન **બદલાવી** (f), મેં વાળ **કપાવ્યા** (m pl), મેં કપડાં **ધોવડાવ્યાં** (n pl). It's also how English verbs are used: **રિપેર કરાવવું, ચેક કરાવવું, રિચાર્જ કરાવવું**.

**The trap:** મેં વાળ **કાપ્યા** means *I* cut the hair, with my own scissors. At the barber's it's always **કપાવ્યા**. In the same way you **open** a bank account with ખોલાવવું and **pay in** money with જમા **કરાવવું**, because the bank does the work.

grammar.title: Verb families: બનવું → બનાવવું → બનાવડાવવું
grammar.body:
Many Gujarati verbs come in sets of three that share a root:

**1. it happens** (no doer): **બનવું** 'get made, be ready'
**2. someone does it**: **બનાવવું** 'make'
**3. someone gets it done**: **બનાવડાવવું** 'get it made'

ડ્રેસ **બની** ગયો — the outfit is ready.
દરજીએ ડ્રેસ **બનાવ્યો** — the tailor made the outfit.
મેં ડ્રેસ **બનાવડાવ્યો** — I had the outfit made.

More families you'll need for errands:
ખૂલવું / ખોલવું / ખોલાવવું — open
કપાવું / કાપવું / કપાવવું — cut
ધોવાવું / ધોવું / ધોવડાવવું — wash
સિવાવું / સીવવું / સિવડાવવું — stitch
ઠીક થવું / ઠીક કરવું / ઠીક કરાવવું — get fixed / fix / have fixed

The first verb of many families is made with **-આ-** (ધોવાવું, સિવાવું, કપાવું): it's Gujarati's 'gets done' form, the same one you met in **ખોવાઈ ગયું** 'got lost' and **ચોરાઈ ગયો** 'got stolen'.

When you ask about the **thing** — is it ready, fixed, washed — use the first verb, usually with **જવું**: **ક્યારે બની જશે?** 'when will it be ready?', **ફોન ઠીક થઈ ગયો?** 'is the phone fixed?', **કપડાં ધોવાઈ ગયાં?** 'are the clothes washed?'.

**The trap:** the first verb never takes the ergative, because nobody is doing anything in that sentence: ડ્રેસ **બની ગયો**, never 'ડ્રેસે બનાવ્યો'. And 'it isn't ready yet' is **હજી નથી બન્યો**, not 'નથી બનાવ્યો' (that means 'I haven't made it').

examples.en: The clothes haven't been washed yet.

grammar.title: મારે … -વું છે: the infinitive agrees with the thing
grammar.body:
You know **મારે + infinitive + છે** for 'I need to / want to' (unit 15): **મારે જવું છે** 'I need to go'. Errands are full of it.

When the infinitive has an **object**, the infinitive changes its ending to agree with that object, exactly like an adjective:

masculine → **-વો**: મારે ફોન રિપેર **કરાવવો** છે
feminine → **-વી**: મારે દાઢી **કરાવવી** છે
neuter → **-વું**: મારે ફૉર્મ **ભરવું** છે
masculine plural → **-વા**: મારે પૈસા **ઉપાડવા** છે, મારે વાળ **કપાવવા** છે
neuter plural → **-વાં**: મારે કપડાં **ધોવડાવવાં** છે

With no object (or with a verb like જવું, આવવું) it stays **-વું**: મારે બેંકમાં **જવું** છે.

The same agreement happens with **પડશે** 'will have to' and **જોઈએ** 'should': **સ્ક્રીન બદલાવવી પડશે** 'the screen will have to be replaced'.

**The trap:** learn the gender of the thing along with the word, because you'll need it here. પૈસા and વાળ are always plural in Gujarati, so they take **-વા**: never 'મારે પૈસા ઉપાડવું છે'. In fast speech you'll sometimes hear -વું everywhere, but the agreeing form is what people expect.

examples.en: I want to buy a new phone.
I need to fill in a form.
I want to take a few photos.
I need to get some clothes washed.

culture: Most errands in a Gujarati town happen at small neighbourhood shops where the same people know you for years: the mobile shop that does top-ups, SIMs and screen repairs; the **દરજી** whose shop is buried in fabric in the weeks before Navratri, when everyone wants a new **ચણિયાચોળી** or kediyu stitched; the **ઇસ્ત્રીવાળો** ironing clothes with a heavy charcoal or electric iron at a table by the society gate; and the local **વાળંદ**. Shopkeepers are **ભાઈ** or **બેન** (or **કાકા**, **માસી** if older), and with the ones you see every week you'll soon switch from **તમે** to a friendly **તું**; in a bank or a smart salon stay with **તમે**. Services are rarely bargained over, but always ask **ક્યારે મળશે?** and expect **કાલે ચોક્કસ** ('tomorrow, for sure') to mean 'probably the day after'. Almost everywhere you can pay by UPI: just ask **સ્કૅન કરી દઉં?** 'shall I scan?'. In the diaspora — Leicester, Wembley, Edison in New Jersey — many chemists, post-office counters and corner shops are Gujarati-run, and a **કેમ છો?** at the counter often gets you a smile and a chat.

tip.title: મારે પૈસા ઉપાડવા છે — I need to…
tip.body:
- **મારે + infinitive + છે** = 'I need to': મારે બેંકમાં **જવું** છે.
- With an object, the infinitive agrees with the **thing**: ફૉર્મ **ભરવું** (n) · ફોન **કરાવવો** (m) · ફી **ભરવી** (f) · પૈસા **ઉપાડવા** (pl).
- પૈસા is always plural, so it's always **-વા**.

lessons.title: Phone trouble: SIMs and repairs

tip.title: Getting it done: કરાવવું
tip.body:
- To have **someone else** do it, add **-આવ-** to the root: કરવું → **કરાવવું**, બદલવું → **બદલાવવું**.
- English verbs go with it: **રિપેર કરાવવું**, **રિચાર્જ કરાવવું**.
- In the past it agrees with the thing: મેં ફોન રિપેર **કરાવ્યો** (m), સ્ક્રીન **બદલાવી** (f).
- રિપેર **કરે છે** = does it himself; રિપેર **કરાવે છે** = gets it done.

new: મને નવું સિમ કાર્ડ જોઈએ છે.

sentences.native: ફોન બગડી ગયો, રિપેર કરાવવો પડશે.
sentences.roman: fon bagḍī gayo, riper karāvvo paḍshe.
sentences.en: The phone's stopped working, I'll have to get it repaired.

sentences.native: મેં ગયા અઠવાડિયે જ ફોન રિપેર કરાવ્યો હતો.
sentences.roman: meṃ gayā aṭhvāḍiye j fon riper karāvyo hato.
sentences.en: I only got my phone repaired last week.
I want to get my phone screen replaced.
Where did you get your screen replaced? (informal)

sentences.native: મેં નવું સિમ કાર્ડ ચાલુ કરાવ્યું.
sentences.roman: meṃ navuṃ sim kārḍ chālu karāvyuṃ.
sentences.en: I got a new SIM card activated.

sentences.native: હું અહીં જ રિચાર્જ કરાવું છું.
sentences.roman: huṃ ahīṃ j richārj karāvuṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: I always get my top-ups done here.

sentences.native: તમે ફોન ક્યાં રિપેર કરાવો છો?
sentences.roman: tame fon kyāṃ riper karāvo chho?
sentences.en: Where do you get your phone repaired?

sentences.native: મારો ભાઈ ફોન જાતે રિપેર કરે છે.
sentences.roman: māro bhāī fon jāte riper kare chhe.
sentences.en: My brother repairs phones himself.

sentences.native: હું આજે સાંજે ફોન રિપેર કરાવીશ.
sentences.roman: huṃ āje sāṃje fon riper karāvīsh.
sentences.en: I'll get the phone repaired this evening.
How much will the repair be?
You'll need your passport for the SIM card.
The signal isn't good here.

lessons.title: At the tailor's: is it ready yet?

tip.title: બની ગયું? — is it ready?
tip.body:
- Verbs come in threes: **બનવું** 'be made, be ready' → **બનાવવું** 'make' → **બનાવડાવવું** 'get made'. Also સિવાવું / સીવવું / **સિવડાવવું**.
- To ask about the **thing**, use the first verb with જવું: **બની ગયો?** **સિવાઈ જશે?**
- 'Not ready yet' = **હજી નથી બન્યો** (not બનાવ્યો).
- **સુધીમાં** = 'by': શનિવાર **સુધીમાં**.

sentences.en: I want to get an outfit stitched.
Is my outfit ready?
It isn't ready yet, come tomorrow.

sentences.native: મેં આ શર્ટ અહીં જ બનાવડાવ્યું હતું.
sentences.roman: meṃ ā sharṭ ahīṃ j banāvḍāvyuṃ hatuṃ.
sentences.en: I had this shirt made right here.
Where did you get this outfit made? (informal)
Will it be ready by Diwali?
It'll be stitched by Saturday.

sentences.native: આ દરજી બહુ સરસ સીવે છે.
sentences.roman: ā darjī bahu saras sīve chhe.
sentences.en: This tailor sews really well.

sentences.native: દરજી કહે છે કે ડ્રેસ સોમવાર સુધીમાં બની જશે.
sentences.roman: darjī kahe chhe ke ḍres somvār sudhīmāṃ banī jashe.
sentences.en: The tailor says the outfit will be ready by Monday.
The tailor took my measurements.

lessons.title: At the barber's or the parlour

tip.title: Cutting it yourself, or getting it cut?
tip.body:
- At the barber's it's always the causative: **વાળ કપાવવા** 'get a haircut', **દાઢી કરાવવી** 'get a shave'.
- મેં વાળ **કાપ્યા** means *you* held the scissors!
- વાળ is plural: મેં વાળ **કપાવ્યા**, મારે વાળ **કપાવવા** છે.
- Men go to the **વાળંદ** or a salon, women usually to a **પાર્લર**.

sentences.en: I only got my hair cut yesterday.

sentences.native: તારા વાળ સરસ લાગે છે! ક્યાં કપાવ્યા?
sentences.roman: tārā vāḷ saras lāge chhe! kyāṃ kapāvyā?
sentences.en: Your hair looks great! Where did you get it cut?
I want a shave as well.

sentences.native: મારી બહેન પાર્લરમાં વાળ કપાવે છે.
sentences.roman: mārī bahen pārlarmāṃ vāḷ kapāve chhe.
sentences.en: My sister gets her hair cut at the parlour.

sentences.native: અહીં વાળ કપાવવાના કેટલા થાય છે?
sentences.roman: ahīṃ vāḷ kapāvvānā keṭlā thāy chhe?
sentences.en: How much is a haircut here?

sentences.native: પપ્પા રોજ દાઢી જાતે કરે છે.
sentences.roman: pappā roj dāḍhī jāte kare chhe.
sentences.en: Dad shaves himself every day.
I got my son's hair cut.

sentences.native: આજે વાળંદની દુકાનમાં બહુ ભીડ છે.
sentences.roman: āje vāḷandnī dukānmāṃ bahu bhīḍ chhe.
sentences.en: The barber's is really busy today.
Don't make it too short at the front.

sentences.native: મારે લગ્ન પહેલાં પાર્લરમાં જવું છે.
sentences.roman: māre lagna pahelāṃ pārlarmāṃ javuṃ chhe.
sentences.en: I want to go to the parlour before the wedding.

tip.title: Without, and "do it for me"
tip.body:
- Clothes go to the **ધોબી**: **કપડાં ધોવડાવવાં**, **ઇસ્ત્રી કરાવવી**.
- 'Without' is **વગર** after the noun: ખાંડ **વગર**, ચિઠ્ઠી **વગર**.
- 'Do it for me' is the verb + **આપજો**: ઇસ્ત્રી **કરી આપજો** 'please iron it for me'.

sentences.en: I got all the clothes washed.
Are the clothes washed?

sentences.native: મારે ઑફિસ માટે શર્ટને ઇસ્ત્રી કરાવવી છે.
sentences.roman: māre ofis māṭe sharṭne istrī karāvvī chhe.
sentences.en: I need to get my shirt ironed for the office.

sentences.native: આ સાડીને ઇસ્ત્રી કરી આપજો, કાલે લગ્નમાં જવું છે.
sentences.roman: ā sāḍīne istrī karī āpjo, kāle lagnamāṃ javuṃ chhe.
sentences.en: Please iron this sari for me, I've got a wedding tomorrow.
Tea without sugar, please.

sentences.native: ડૉક્ટરની ચિઠ્ઠી વગર આ દવા નહીં મળે.
sentences.roman: ḍokṭarnī chiṭṭhī vagar ā davā nahīṃ maḷe.
sentences.en: You can't get this medicine without a doctor's prescription.

sentences.native: ચા વગર મારો દિવસ શરૂ નથી થતો.
sentences.roman: chā vagar māro divas sharū nathī thato.
sentences.en: My day doesn't start without tea.
These clothes need to go to the dhobi.
How much for the ironing?
Is there a chemist nearby?
Please give me all the medicines on this prescription.

lessons.title: Sending a parcel

tip.title: Arrive and deliver: પહોંચવું → પહોંચાડવું
tip.body:
- The parcel **arrives**: પાર્સલ **પહોંચશે**, **પહોંચી ગયું**.
- Someone **delivers** it: કુરિયરવાળો પાર્સલ **પહોંચાડશે**.
- You **get it sent**: મેં પાર્સલ **મોકલાવ્યું** (agrees with the thing).
- Ask: **કેટલા દિવસમાં પહોંચશે?**

new: મારે આ પાર્સલ મુંબઈ મોકલવું છે. કેટલા થશે?

sentences.en: I had some sweets sent for Mum.
How many days will the parcel take to arrive?
The courier will deliver the parcel tomorrow.

sentences.native: મારે આ પાર્સલ કાલ સુધીમાં સુરત પહોંચાડવું છે.
sentences.roman: māre ā pārsal kāl sudhīmāṃ Surat pahoṃchāḍvuṃ chhe.
sentences.en: I need to get this parcel to Surat by tomorrow.
The shopkeeper delivers things to your door.
I sent my passport by courier.
Has the parcel arrived?
Do you courier to London?
What's in the parcel?
